body:
Fines for minor offences, such as parking on a double yellow line, should be calculated according to the income of the person who breaks the rule, so that a penalty hurts a wealthy driver as much as a poor one.

Do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Courts should give people who commit minor offences unpaid work for the community instead of a fine, because the work benefits the people and places their actions have affected.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Schools should teach children how to create secure passwords and protect their personal information as a regular part of the curriculum, so that they are less likely to become victims of online crime.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some supermarkets have started to remove their self-service tills and bring back checkouts run by staff, partly because the machines make it easy for customers to leave without paying for everything.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Police forces should spend their budgets on officers who walk the streets and know local residents, rather than on computer systems and other new technology.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people believe that speed cameras are the most effective way to persuade drivers to slow down near schools and in residential streets. Others argue that they are mainly a way for local authorities to raise money from motorists.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people think that heavy fines are the only effective way to stop people dropping litter in parks and streets. Others believe that education, better bins and local pride would achieve more.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people think that young people under the age of 16 should not be allowed in town centres after 9 p.m. unless an adult is with them. Others believe such a rule would punish the majority for the behaviour of a few.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Governments should set a strict legal limit on noise in residential streets after 11 p.m., even if this forces bars, building firms and delivery companies to finish work earlier.

Do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Governments are increasingly placing higher taxes on luxury goods such as yachts, designer handbags and sports cars, rather than on everyday items that ordinary families need.

Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Public money is limited, so governments must decide whether to fund museums, theatres and libraries or to spend it on roads, bridges and public transport.

Why do some governments give roads a higher priority than the arts?

Is this a positive or negative development for the long-term well-being of a country?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

In some countries, government departments and the jobs that go with them are being moved out of the capital city and into smaller towns.

Why might governments choose to do this?

Is this a positive or negative development for the country as a whole?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

In many areas, very few residents respond when their local council asks for views on plans such as new housing estates, road schemes or shopping centres.

Why is this happening?

What can be done to encourage more people to take part in decisions about their local area?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people believe that every citizen should be required to carry a national identity card, because it makes public services more efficient and helps the state protect its people. Others argue that such cards threaten personal freedom and privacy.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some local councils now offer small rewards, such as vouchers for local shops, to residents who return lost property or report problems in their neighbourhood.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

A growing number of local councils are handing the day-to-day running of libraries, parks and community halls over to groups of local residents who work unpaid.

To what extent do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
